cards.explanation: The word is intoxicated. The angel says those who dwell on the earth were “…intoxicated with the wine of her immorality.” (Revelation 17:2) Picture somebody who can't walk a straight line, and you've got the idea. I think it's the angel's way of showing how swept up they were.
The answer is False. The text says the scarlet beast was “…covered with blasphemous names…” (Revelation 17:3) That's not a name tag anybody would want.

The answer is purple and scarlet. The woman is dressed in purple and scarlet, with gold and precious stones and pearls on top (Revelation 17:4). Scarlet is also the color of the beast she sits on (Revelation 17:3). Fancy from head to toe, friends, and the passage keeps showing us what's under the fancy.

The answer is abominations and impurities. She held “…a golden cup full of abominations and the impurities of her sexual immorality.” (Revelation 17:4) A golden cup sounds like something you'd want to drink from. The gold is on the outside, and what's inside is the problem.

The city is Babylon. The name on her forehead begins “BABYLON THE GREAT…” (Revelation 17:5) A name written right on the forehead, so there's no hiding it. And the text calls it a mysterious name, so we stay tuned for what the angel says about her.

The answer is True. The whole name reads “BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF PROSTITUTES AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.” (Revelation 17:5) The name goes on past the city, and every word of it is there, friends.

The answer is True. The angel asks, “Why are you so amazed?” and keeps going. He says, “I will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her, which has the seven heads and ten horns.” (Revelation 17:7) He doesn't leave John hanging.

The word is destruction. The beast “…is about to come up out of the Abyss and go to its destruction.” (Revelation 17:8) Big entrance, rough exit. The angel says it again a few verses later, that the beast “…is going into destruction.” (Revelation 17:11)

The answer is those not written in the Book of Life. The angel says those who dwell on the earth “…whose names were not written in the Book of Life from the foundation of the world will marvel when they see the beast…” (Revelation 17:8) That's who does the marveling, friends. And what they marvel at is the beast.

The answer is False. Of the seven kings, the one who has not yet come “…must remain for only a little while.” (Revelation 17:10) The angel says he comes, and then his stay is short. The passage doesn't give a number, so a little while is the whole answer.

The number is eight. The angel says the beast “…is an eighth king, who belongs to the other seven and is going into destruction.” (Revelation 17:11) Seven kings, and the beast makes eight. His ending is the same as before: destruction.

The answer is one hour. The ten kings “…will receive one hour of authority as kings along with the beast.” (Revelation 17:12) That's a short shift, shorter than a lot of meetings. They haven't even received a kingdom yet, and the clock is already tiny.
The word is beast. The angel says, “These kings have one purpose: to yield their power and authority to the beast.” (Revelation 17:13) All ten, one purpose, and the beast is where it all goes.

The answer is True. The angel says the ten kings “…will make war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will triumph over them…” (Revelation 17:14) Ten kings, a war, and the Lamb still triumphs. The story isn't over yet, though, so there's more to come.
The reason is that He rules over all lords and kings. The Lamb will triumph “…because He is Lord of lords and King of kings…” (Revelation 17:14) Ten kings are big, but He's the King over every king.

The answer is True. The angel says, “…He will be accompanied by His called and chosen and faithful ones.” (Revelation 17:14) Called, chosen and faithful, and they're with Him. That's a good group to be in.

The waters are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues. “The waters you saw, where the prostitute was seated, are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues.” (Revelation 17:15) So no swimming gear needed, friends. The waters are a list of peoples, multitudes, nations and tongues.

The answer is God. The angel says, “For God has put it into their hearts to carry out His purpose by uniting to give their kingdom to the beast, until the words of God are fulfilled.” (Revelation 17:17) The beast and the kings may look like they're running things. The angel says it's God's purpose being carried out.

The answer is the great city that rules the kings of the earth. The angel says, “And the woman you saw is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth.” (Revelation 17:18) So the woman is a city, and it rules over kings. That helps explain why her forehead carried a city's name.
